# Hartwell Supply Co.: what you're looking at

Hartwell is a family-held HVAC/R distributor: about 150 people, twelve branches (Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati, Dayton, Toledo, Akron, Indianapolis, Fort Wayne, Louisville, Lexington, Troy MI and Pittsburgh), selling equipment, parts, refrigerant and supplies to heating and cooling contractors. The records run from 2016 to 2025.

**Its systems, each a separate database copied into the warehouse:**
- **ERP** (`erp_*`): customers and their account managers, the sales reps, products and vendors, sales orders and their lines (how each order arrived and who keyed it), purchase orders, transfers between branches, and returns.
- **Warehouse management** (`wms_*`): every stock movement (opening balances, receipts, sales, transfers, returns) and goods receipts. Stock on hand isn't stored anywhere: it's the running total of the movements.
- **Accounting** (`finance_*`): invoices and their lines, credit memos, customer payments, vendor bills and their lines, and vendor payments.
- **CRM** (`crm_*`): calls and emails to customer service, as logged by whoever took them; and the reps' quotes, with each quote's lines, its outcome (won, lost or expired), a loss reason when the rep entered one, and the order a won quote became.
- **External** (`external_*`): real monthly heating and cooling degree days and residential building permits for each branch's county.

**Days.** `day` is an operating day, about 21 a month; `dim_date` gives the calendar date.

**What isn't here:** profitability by customer, rep or branch; why a return happened; whether an order was keyed correctly; whether a vendor bill was right. Like any real business, those have to be worked out from the records, and some of them can't be.

I've saved `hypotheses.json` with twelve hypotheses. Each one is sized from queries run in this session (q98–q123). I sized them but did not investigate any of them. All margin figures use today's product cost, because the records hold no cost history. The carrying-cost rates (20% on stock, 8% on receivables) are my assumptions, not data.

The biggest finding from sizing is a sharp R-410A equipment problem. Line markdowns grew from about $4.1M in 2022 to $12.0M in 2025 (q103). In 2025, 8,295 of 8,318 R-410A equipment lines were marked down (q109), and that equipment's margin fell from 16.3% to 1.9% (q114). About $7.9M of R-410A stock is still on hand (q113). Parts, supplies and refrigeration had no markdown lines in either year (q109), and markdown rates look the same across order channels and the people keying orders (q106).

| Rank by $ | Hypothesis | Rough size per year | Rank by how well the records can answer it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | H2: margin erosion is customer-discount creep across all categories (margin 27.29% → 22.58%) | up to ~$6.5M margin (q104) | 11 |
| 2 | H1: markdown rise is an R-410A clearance, not people or channels | +$7.9M markdown (q122) | 4 |
| 3 | H8: lost customers concentrate by branch or account manager | ~$8.4M revenue, $1.9M–$2.3M margin (q121, q123) | 9 |
| 4 | H7: stockouts (short lines) lose sales and push customers away | up to ~$2.7M margin (q122) | 12 |
| 5 | H10: excess stock (> 2 years of supply) | ~$2.1M carrying cost at 20% (q108, q121) | 6 |
| 6 | H3: R-410A stock will sell below margin | ~$1.6M margin gap, $7.9M exposure (q113, q122) | 7 |
| 7 | H9: rep win-rate gaps reflect customer discounts; quote markdowns don't win more | $18.5M quote value lost on price; recoverable share not sized (q118, q119) | 10 |
| 8 | H5: bills above the PO paid in full, plus freight | ~$315k + ~$208k (q99, q120) | 3 |
| 9 | H4: duplicate "-R" vendor bills paid | ~$273k (q98) | 1 |
| 10 | H6: goods shipped but never invoiced | ~$285k, 2016–2024 average (q121) | 2 |
| 11 | H11: late customer payments tie up cash | ~$232k at 8% (q107) | 5 |
| 12 | H12: late special orders cause repeat "where is my order" calls | ~1,908 logged hours, no dollar figure (q121) | 8 |

The two rankings deliberately differ. The largest dollar questions (margin erosion, lost customers, stockouts) depend on history the records don't keep: costs, discount changes, backorders and rep assignments. The best-answered ones (duplicate bills, unbilled shipments, bills above PO) are smaller in dollars.

Several are set up to come back "this is fine":
- **H9:** markdowns may buy nothing. Quotes with markdowns win at 42.1–42.7% against 43.0% without (q119).
- **H11:** customer payments look machine-generated rather than real.
- **H12:** the direct staff time involved is small.
- **H1:** if it holds, the extra markdown is the cost of the refrigerant phase-out rather than a controllable leak.

One small inconsistency: excluding the "-R" bills, I count 20,121 bills above PO value (q99), against the orient stage's 20,194.

In 2025, 8,295 of 8,318 R-410A equipment lines were marked down (q109), and that equipment's margin fell from 16.3% to 1.9% (q114). About $7.9M of R-410A stock is still on hand (q113). Parts, supplies and refrigeration had no markdown lines in either year (q109), and markdown rates look the same across order channels and the people keying orders (q106).

Several are set up to come back "this is fine":

- **H12:** the direct staff time involved is small.
- **H1:** if it holds, the extra markdown is the cost of the refrigerant phase-out rather than a controllable leak.
